title: Ternary operator
learningObjectives: Explain ternary operator and write clear, safe expressions.

understand.concept: The conditional (ternary) operator uses condition ? expressionIfTrue : expressionIfFalse. It is an expression that returns one of two values based on the condition. Nested ternaries can become difficult to read and should be avoided when a clearer if/else or function is better.
understand.whyItMatters: Ternary expressions are useful for simple value selection in templates and assignments. Complex branching should use clearer control flow.
understand.analogy: A ternary is a two-way switch that chooses one value based on a condition.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; operator evaluation and coercion follow JavaScript precedence and conversion rules.

explain.narrative: The condition is true, so the expression produces the string Pass.

examples.explanation: The condition is true, so the expression produces the string Pass.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console or page displays the expression results described.

practise.guidedTask: Use a ternary to choose a label based on a boolean. Rewrite a nested ternary as an if/else statement and compare readability.
practise.independentTask: Write a small program that uses the operator or numeric rule in a practical example. Predict results, run the code, and explain any coercion.
hints: Preserve valid falsy values when using defaults.
Validate numeric inputs and check finite results.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Ternary operator</title></head><body>
<script>const score=82;const result=score>=50?'Pass':'Try again';document.body.insertAdjacentText('beforeend',result);</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: Which symbol separates the condition from the true expression in a ternary?
questions.explanation: The question mark follows the condition in a ternary expression.

questions.prompt: What should you do before using a value in a numeric calculation?
options: Assume it is already a valid number
questions.explanation: Explicit conversion and validation prevent invalid or imprecise values from entering calculations.
